AF.name: Afghanistan
facts: Afghanistan is home to the famous Bamiyan Valley, once housing two giant Buddha statues carved in the 6th century.
The national sport of Afghanistan is Buzkashi, a horseback game played with a goat carcass.
Afghanistan has over 200 days of sunshine per year.
The country sits at the crossroads of Central and South Asia, making it historically vital for trade routes.
Afghanistan's Hindu Kush mountain range has peaks over 7,000 meters.

AL.name: Albania
facts: Albania has over 750,000 bunkers built during the communist era — more bunkers per capita than any country.
Mother Teresa, the Nobel Peace Prize winner, was of Albanian origin.
Albania was one of the last European countries to allow private car ownership, banning them until 1991.
The country has a tradition called 'besa' — a code of honor meaning 'to keep the promise.'
Albania's coast has both the Adriatic and Ionian seas.

DZ.name: Algeria
facts: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.
About 80% of Algeria's land area is the Sahara Desert.
The ancient Roman city of Timgad in Algeria is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Algeria gained independence from France in 1962 after a brutal 8-year war.
The country has the 16th-largest oil reserves in the world.

AO.name: Angola
facts: Angola is the second-largest oil producer in sub-Saharan Africa.
The Kalandula Falls in Angola are among the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume.
Angola's capital Luanda was once ranked the most expensive city in the world for expatriates.
The country has a giant sable antelope, found nowhere else on Earth.
Angola shares its name with the Ngola dynasty that once ruled the region.

AR.name: Argentina
facts: Argentina is named after the Latin word for silver — 'argentum.'
The tango dance originated in the working-class neighborhoods of Buenos Aires.
Argentina has the widest avenue in the world — Avenida 9 de Julio has 14 lanes.
Patagonia in southern Argentina contains one of the world's largest dinosaur fossil sites.
Argentina was the first country to use fingerprinting as a method of identification.

AM.name: Armenia
facts: Armenia was the first country to adopt Christianity as a state religion in 301 AD.
The Armenian alphabet was created in 405 AD and has 39 letters.
Armenia is home to the world's oldest leather shoe, dating back 5,500 years.
Chess is a mandatory school subject in Armenia.
Mount Ararat, where Noah's Ark is said to have landed, is visible from Armenia's capital.

AU.name: Australia
facts: Australia is both a country and a continent — the only nation to occupy an entire continent.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth, visible from space.
Australia has more than 10,000 beaches — you could visit a new one every day for 27 years.
The Australian Alps receive more snowfall than the Swiss Alps.
Kangaroos and emus can't walk backward, which is why they're on Australia's coat of arms — symbolizing progress.

AT.name: Austria
facts: Austria's flag is one of the oldest national flags in the world, dating back to 1230.
Vienna has been ranked the world's most livable city multiple times.
The croissant was invented in Vienna to celebrate victory over the Ottoman Empire.
Mozart, Beethoven, Schubert, and Strauss all lived and worked in Vienna.
Austria is 62% covered by the Alps.

AZ.name: Azerbaijan
facts: Azerbaijan is known as the 'Land of Fire' due to natural gas flames that seep from the ground.
Baku's Flame Towers are shaped like flames and are covered in LED screens.
Azerbaijan was the first Muslim-majority country to grant women the right to vote in 1918.
The country has mud volcanoes — more than half of the world's total.
The Maiden Tower in Baku dates back to the 12th century.

BD.name: Bangladesh
facts: Bangladesh is one of the most densely populated countries in the world.
The Sundarbans mangrove forest, shared with India, is the largest in the world and home to Bengal tigers.
The national anthem of Bangladesh was written by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore.
Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China.
Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh has the longest unbroken sea beach in the world at 120 km.

BY.name: Belarus
facts: Belarus is one of the most forested countries in Europe — about 40% is covered by trees.
The European bison, once nearly extinct, roams free in Belarus's Białowieża Forest.
Belarus means 'White Russia' in its language.
Minsk was almost entirely rebuilt after being destroyed in World War II.
Belarus has one of the highest literacy rates in the world at over 99%.

BE.name: Belgium
facts: Belgium produces over 220,000 tonnes of chocolate per year.
The saxophone was invented by Belgian Adolphe Sax in the 1840s.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French, and German.
Brussels is the de facto capital of the European Union.
Belgium has more comic book artists per square mile than any other country.

BJ.name: Benin
facts: Benin is considered the birthplace of Vodun (Voodoo), still widely practiced there.
The Kingdom of Dahomey, based in modern Benin, had an all-female military unit — the Dahomey Amazons.
Benin's Ganvié is the largest lake village in Africa, built entirely on stilts.
The country was formerly known as Dahomey until 1975.
Benin has one of the highest rates of twin births in the world.

BO.name: Bolivia
facts: Bolivia has 37 official languages, one of the most in any country.
The Salar de Uyuni is the world's largest salt flat, covering 10,582 square kilometers.
La Paz, Bolivia's administrative capital, is the highest capital city in the world at 3,640 meters.
Bolivia is named after Simón Bolívar, the South American independence leader.
Bolivia is one of only two landlocked countries in South America.

BR.name: Brazil
facts: Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas.
The Amazon Rainforest produces about 20% of the world's oxygen.
Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup a record 5 times.
São Paulo has the largest Japanese population outside Japan.
Brazil's coastline stretches over 7,400 km — longer than the distance from New York to London.

BG.name: Bulgaria
facts: Bulgaria is the oldest country in Europe that hasn't changed its name since it was first established in 681 AD.
Bulgarians shake their head for 'yes' and nod for 'no' — the opposite of most countries.
The Cyrillic alphabet was developed in Bulgaria in the 9th century.
Bulgarian yogurt contains a unique bacteria — Lactobacillus bulgaricus — found nowhere else.
Bulgaria has been producing rose oil for perfumes for over 300 years.

KH.name: Cambodia
facts: Cambodia's Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world.
The Cambodian flag is the only national flag to feature a building (Angkor Wat).
The Tonlé Sap lake doubles in size during the monsoon season.
Cambodia's Khmer Empire once controlled much of Southeast Asia.
Cambodia uses the US dollar alongside its own currency in everyday transactions.

CM.name: Cameroon
facts: Cameroon is called 'Africa in miniature' because it contains all of Africa's major climates and vegetation.
Mount Cameroon is the highest peak in West Africa and is an active volcano.
The name 'Cameroon' comes from Portuguese explorers who named it 'Rio dos Camarões' (River of Shrimp).
Cameroon has over 250 different ethnic groups.
Cameroon's football team, the Indomitable Lions, was the first African team to reach a World Cup quarter-final.

CA.name: Canada
facts: Canada has the longest coastline in the world at over 202,080 km.
Canada has more lakes than all other countries combined.
The Trans-Canada Highway is one of the longest national highways in the world at 7,821 km.
Canada produces 71% of the world's maple syrup.
The Canadian territory of Nunavut is larger than Western Europe but has a population of only about 40,000.

CL.name: Chile
facts: Chile is the longest north-south country in the world, stretching 4,300 km.
The Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest place on Earth — some areas haven't seen rain in over 400 years.
Chile has the world's largest swimming pool at the San Alfonso del Mar resort — over 1 km long.
Easter Island (Rapa Nui), with its famous Moai statues, belongs to Chile.
Chile was the first South American country to legalize same-sex marriage.

CN.name: China
facts: The Great Wall of China stretches over 21,000 km and took more than 2,000 years to build.
China invented paper, printing, gunpowder, and the compass — known as the Four Great Inventions.
All pandas in the world belong to China — those in foreign zoos are on loan.
China has the world's fastest commercial train — the Shanghai Maglev reaches 431 km/h.
The Terracotta Army in Xi'an has over 8,000 unique soldier statues, each with a different face.

CO.name: Colombia
facts: Colombia is the only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific and Caribbean.
Colombia produces more emeralds than any other country — about 70-90% of the world's supply.
The country is named after Christopher Columbus, though he never set foot there.
Colombia is the second most biodiverse country in the world after Brazil.
Bogotá's Ciclovía closes 120 km of roads to cars every Sunday for cyclists and pedestrians.

CD.name: DR Congo
facts: The Congo River is the deepest river in the world, reaching depths of over 220 meters.
DR Congo contains over half of Africa's tropical rainforest.
The country has massive deposits of coltan, essential for making smartphones and laptops.
Kinshasa and Brazzaville are the two closest capital cities in the world, separated only by the Congo River.
DR Congo is the largest country in sub-Saharan Africa.

CR.name: Costa Rica
facts: Costa Rica has no army — it was abolished in 1948 and the budget redirected to education and healthcare.
The country contains 5% of the world's biodiversity despite being only 0.03% of the planet's surface.
Costa Rica consistently ranks among the happiest countries in the world.
'Pura Vida' (Pure Life) is the national motto and greeting.
Costa Rica generates over 98% of its electricity from renewable sources.

CU.name: Cuba
facts: Cuba has one of the highest literacy rates in the world at 99.8%.
Classic American cars from the 1950s still fill Cuban streets because of a decades-long trade embargo.
Cuba has more doctors per capita than most developed nations.
The island was the first place Christopher Columbus landed in the Americas in 1492.
Cuban cigars are considered the finest in the world due to the island's unique soil.

CZ.name: Czechia
facts: Czechia has the highest beer consumption per capita in the world.
Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle in the world according to Guinness World Records.
The word 'robot' was coined by Czech writer Karel Čapek in 1920.
The soft contact lens was invented by Czech chemist Otto Wichterle.
Czechia is one of the least religious countries in the world.

DK.name: Denmark
facts: Denmark's flag (Dannebrog) is the oldest state flag in the world still in use, dating to 1219.
LEGO was invented in Denmark — the name comes from 'leg godt' meaning 'play well.'
No point in Denmark is more than 52 km from the sea.
Denmark is consistently ranked as one of the happiest countries in the world.
The concept of 'hygge' — Danish coziness and comfortable living — has become famous worldwide.

EC.name: Ecuador
facts: Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through the country.
The Galápagos Islands, belonging to Ecuador, inspired Darwin's theory of evolution.
Ecuador was the first country to constitutionally recognize the rights of nature.
Panama hats actually originate from Ecuador, not Panama.
Ecuador uses the US dollar as its official currency.

EG.name: Egypt
facts: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest man-made structure for nearly 4,000 years.
Ancient Egyptians invented one of the first writing systems — hieroglyphics.
Egypt's Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea and handles 12% of global trade.
Cairo is the largest city in Africa and the Arab world.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.

ET.name: Ethiopia
facts: Ethiopia is the only African country that was never colonized.
Ethiopia follows a unique calendar that is 7-8 years behind the Gregorian calendar and has 13 months.
Coffee was discovered in Ethiopia — legend says a goat herder noticed his goats dancing after eating coffee berries.
Lucy, one of the oldest known human ancestors (3.2 million years), was found in Ethiopia.
Ethiopia's Danakil Depression is one of the hottest inhabited places on Earth.

FI.name: Finland
facts: Finland has over 3 million saunas for a population of 5.6 million — roughly one per household.
Finland is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' but actually has 188,000 lakes.
Finland's education system is ranked among the best in the world, with no standardized tests.
Finland was the first country in Europe to give women the right to vote in 1906.
Santa Claus is officially recognized as living in Rovaniemi, Finland.

FR.name: France
facts: France is the most visited country in the world with over 89 million tourists annually.
The Eiffel Tower was meant to be temporary — it was built for the 1889 World's Fair.
France has the most time zones of any country (12) due to its overseas territories.
French law requires that at least 40% of music on French radio must be of French origin.
The Louvre in Paris is the most visited art museum in the world.

DE.name: Germany
facts: Germany has over 1,500 different beers and hosts the world-famous Oktoberfest.
The printing press was invented by Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz, Germany around 1440.
Germany's Autobahn has sections with no speed limit.
Berlin has more bridges than Venice — approximately 960.
Germany is the birthplace of Kindergarten — the word means 'children's garden.'

GH.name: Ghana
facts: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule in 1957.
Ghana is the second-largest producer of cocoa in the world.
Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world by surface area.
Ghana is known for its colorful fantasy coffins, shaped like animals, cars, or symbols of the deceased's life.
The name 'Ghana' means 'Warrior King' in the Soninke language.

GR.name: Greece
facts: Greece is considered the birthplace of democracy, philosophy, and the Olympic Games.
Greece has more archaeological museums than any other country in the world.
The Greek language has been spoken for over 3,400 years, making it one of the oldest living languages.
Greece has over 6,000 islands, but only about 227 are inhabited.
The marathon race is named after a Greek soldier who ran from Marathon to Athens — about 42 km.

HU.name: Hungary
facts: The Rubik's Cube was invented by Hungarian professor Ernő Rubik in 1974.
Budapest has the largest thermal water cave system in the world.
Hungary has won more Olympic gold medals per capita than most countries.
The Hungarian language is unrelated to any neighboring country's language.
Budapest's Parliament Building is the third largest in the world.

IS.name: Iceland
facts: Iceland has no army, navy, or air force.
About 60% of Iceland's population lives in the capital area of Reykjavik.
Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was established in 930 AD — one of the oldest in the world.
Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, with parts on both the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.
There are no mosquitoes in Iceland.

IN.name: India
facts: India has the most post offices of any country in the world — over 155,000.
The number zero was invented in India by mathematician Aryabhata.
India is the world's largest producer of spices and milk.
The Kumbh Mela gathering in India is visible from space due to the sheer number of people.
India's space program has sent missions to the Moon and Mars at costs lower than many Hollywood films.

ID.name: Indonesia
facts: Indonesia is the largest archipelago in the world with over 17,000 islands.
Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizards, are found only in Indonesia.
Indonesia has the third-largest tropical rainforest in the world after Brazil and Congo.
Bali, one of Indonesia's islands, is one of the world's top tourist destinations.
Indonesia is the world's largest island country and the 4th most populous nation.

IR.name: Iran
facts: Iran is home to one of the world's oldest civilizations, dating back to 3200 BCE.
The Persian Empire was the largest empire in ancient history, spanning three continents.
Iran has 27 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
The concept of the postal system was invented in ancient Persia (modern-day Iran).
Tehran's Grand Bazaar is one of the oldest and largest bazaars in the Middle East.

IQ.name: Iraq
facts: Iraq is home to Mesopotamia, often called the 'Cradle of Civilization.'
The ancient city of Babylon, with its famous hanging gardens, was located in modern Iraq.
Writing was invented in Mesopotamia (Iraq) around 3400 BCE using cuneiform.
Iraq has the fifth-largest proven oil reserves in the world.
The Tigris and Euphrates rivers, which run through Iraq, supported the earliest known civilizations.

IE.name: Ireland
facts: Ireland has no snakes — legend credits Saint Patrick with driving them out.
Halloween originated in Ireland from the ancient Celtic festival of Samhain.
Ireland is home to over 30,000 castles and ruins.
The harp, not the shamrock, is Ireland's official national symbol.
Ireland's population is still lower than it was before the Great Famine of the 1840s.

IL.name: Israel
facts: Israel has more museums per capita than any other country.
Hebrew was a dead language for 1,700 years before being revived in Israel.
The Dead Sea, bordering Israel and Jordan, is the lowest point on Earth's surface.
Israel leads the world in recycled water use — over 85% of wastewater is recycled.
Israel has more startups per capita than any other country.

IT.name: Italy
facts: Italy has the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites of any country in the world.
The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is the oldest university in continuous operation.
Italy is home to two independent countries within its borders: Vatican City and San Marino.
Italians invented the piano, espresso machine, and eyeglasses.
The Colosseum in Rome could hold 50,000–80,000 spectators.

JP.name: Japan
facts: Japan is made up of 6,852 islands.
Japan has more than 1,500 earthquakes per year.
Vending machines in Japan sell everything from hot meals to umbrellas — there are over 5 million.
Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains have an average delay of only 17 seconds.
The Japanese concept of 'forest bathing' (shinrin-yoku) is a recognized form of stress therapy.

JO.name: Jordan
facts: Petra, Jordan's famous ancient city carved into rock, is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
Jordan borders the Dead Sea, the lowest point on Earth at 430 meters below sea level.
Wadi Rum desert in Jordan was used as a filming location for 'The Martian' and 'Lawrence of Arabia.'
Jordan is one of the most water-scarce countries in the world.
Amman was originally built on seven hills, like Rome.

KZ.name: Kazakhstan
facts: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.
The Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan was the launch site for the first human space flight.
Apples are believed to have originated in Kazakhstan — the name 'Almaty' means 'Father of Apples.'
Kazakhstan spans two continents: Europe and Asia.
The country is the 9th largest in the world by area.

KE.name: Kenya
facts: Kenya is named after Mount Kenya, the second-highest peak in Africa.
The Great Rift Valley runs through Kenya, visible from space.
Kenya dominates long-distance running — Kenyan athletes have won countless Olympic and marathon medals.
M-Pesa, the world's leading mobile money service, was invented in Kenya.
The annual wildebeest migration in Kenya's Masai Mara is one of the greatest wildlife spectacles on Earth.

KR.name: South Korea
facts: South Korea has the fastest average internet speed in the world.
K-pop and Korean dramas (K-dramas) have become a global cultural phenomenon.
South Korea's Samsung produces about 20% of the country's GDP.
The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was specifically designed to be easy to learn.
South Korea has a 'Black Day' (April 14) where single people eat black bean noodles to commiserate.

KW.name: Kuwait
facts: The Kuwaiti Dinar is the highest-valued currency unit in the world.
Kuwait has no rivers or permanent bodies of fresh water.
Kuwait was one of the first Gulf states to establish a parliament.
The country gets almost all its fresh water from desalination plants.
Kuwait has some of the hottest temperatures ever recorded — up to 54°C.

LB.name: Lebanon
facts: Lebanon's cedar tree is on its flag and has been famous since ancient times.
Beirut has been destroyed and rebuilt 7 times throughout history.
Byblos in Lebanon is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
The Phoenicians, who invented the alphabet, came from modern-day Lebanon.
Lebanon is smaller than Connecticut but has 18 recognized religious sects.

MY.name: Malaysia
facts: Malaysia's Petronas Twin Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.
Malaysia has one of the oldest tropical rainforests in the world — over 130 million years old.
The country is split into two parts separated by the South China Sea.
Malaysia is one of the world's top producers of palm oil and rubber.
The Rafflesia, the world's largest flower, can be found in Malaysian Borneo.

MX.name: Mexico
facts: Mexico City was built on the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán.
Mexico introduced chocolate, chili peppers, and corn to the world.
Mexico has 35 UNESCO World Heritage Sites — more than any other country in the Americas.
The Chichén Itzá pyramid creates a shadow of a serpent during the spring equinox.
Mexico City is sinking at a rate of about 50 cm per year due to water extraction from underground.

MA.name: Morocco
facts: Morocco is home to the world's oldest university — the University of al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859 AD.
The Sahara Desert covers a large portion of southern Morocco.
Morocco is only 14 km from Spain across the Strait of Gibraltar.
Fez, Morocco has the world's oldest tannery still in operation.
Morocco was the first country to recognize the United States as an independent nation in 1777.

NP.name: Nepal
facts: Nepal is the only country in the world with a non-rectangular flag.
Mount Everest, the tallest mountain on Earth at 8,849m, is in Nepal.
Nepal has never been colonized by a foreign power.
Lumbini, Nepal is the birthplace of the Buddha.
Nepal's flag is made of two stacked triangles representing the Himalayas and two religions: Hinduism and Buddhism.

NL.name: Netherlands
facts: About one-third of the Netherlands is below sea level.
The Netherlands has more bicycles than people — about 23 million bikes for 17.8 million people.
Amsterdam has over 1,200 bridges and 165 canals.
The Dutch are the tallest people in the world on average.
The Netherlands invented the stock exchange (Amsterdam Stock Exchange, 1602).

NZ.name: New Zealand
facts: New Zealand was the first country to give all women the right to vote in 1893.
There are more sheep than people in New Zealand — about 6 sheep per person.
New Zealand has no native land mammals (except bats) — it was dominated by birds before human arrival.
The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit trilogies were filmed entirely in New Zealand.
New Zealand is one of the last major landmasses settled by humans — around 1250-1300 AD.

NG.name: Nigeria
facts: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa and the 6th most populous in the world.
Nollywood (Nigeria's film industry) produces more movies annually than Hollywood.
Nigeria has over 500 different ethnic groups and over 520 languages.
Lagos is the largest city in Africa with an estimated population of over 20 million.
Nigeria is Africa's largest economy and its biggest oil exporter.

KP.name: North Korea
facts: North Korea uses its own calendar, called the Juche calendar, starting from 1912.
North Korea and South Korea are technically still at war — only an armistice was signed, not a peace treaty.
Pyongyang has a 105-story pyramid-shaped hotel (Ryugyong Hotel) that has never opened.
North Korea has its own intranet called Kwangmyong, separate from the global internet.
The DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) between North and South Korea has become an accidental wildlife refuge.

NO.name: Norway
facts: Norway has the world's longest road tunnel — the Lærdalstunnelen at 24.5 km.
Norway's Government Pension Fund is the largest sovereign wealth fund in the world.
The Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis) are visible in northern Norway.
Norway introduced salmon sushi to Japan in the 1980s.
Norway knighted a penguin — Brigadier Sir Nils Olav III at Edinburgh Zoo.

PK.name: Pakistan
facts: Pakistan has the world's second-highest mountain — K2 at 8,611 meters.
The ancient Indus Valley civilization, one of the world's oldest, was in modern Pakistan.
Pakistan's Karakoram Highway is one of the highest paved international roads in the world.
Pakistan is the world's fourth-largest producer of cotton.
The national sport of Pakistan is field hockey, in which they have won multiple Olympic medals.

PE.name: Peru
facts: Machu Picchu, the ancient Inca city, is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
Peru has 90 different microclimates, making it one of the most diverse countries on Earth.
The potato originated in Peru — there are over 3,000 varieties grown there.
Lake Titicaca, shared with Bolivia, is the highest navigable lake in the world.
The Nazca Lines in Peru are ancient geoglyphs visible only from the air.

PH.name: Philippines
facts: The Philippines is made up of 7,641 islands.
The Philippines is the texting capital of the world — Filipinos send billions of texts monthly.
Jeepneys, colorfully decorated former military jeeps, are the most popular form of public transportation.
The Chocolate Hills of Bohol are over 1,200 cone-shaped hills that turn brown in dry season.
The Philippines has the longest Christmas celebration in the world — starting in September.

PL.name: Poland
facts: Marie Curie, the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, was born in Poland.
Poland's Białowieża Forest is one of the last and largest primeval forests in Europe.
The Polish constitution of 1791 was the first modern constitution in Europe.
Kraków's St. Mary's Basilica plays a trumpet call every hour that stops mid-note — commemorating a 13th-century watchman shot by invaders.
Poland is the world's largest exporter of amber.

PT.name: Portugal
facts: Portugal is the oldest nation-state in Europe, with borders largely unchanged since 1249.
The Portuguese Empire was the first global empire and the longest-lasting European colonial empire.
Portugal decriminalized all drugs in 2001 and saw drug abuse rates drop significantly.
Lisbon is older than Rome — it's one of the oldest cities in Western Europe.
Portugal's Vasco da Gama Bridge is the longest bridge in Europe at 12.3 km.

RO.name: Romania
facts: Bram Stoker's Dracula was inspired by Vlad the Impaler, a Romanian prince.
Romania's Palace of the Parliament is the heaviest building in the world.
The Danube Delta in Romania is Europe's largest wetland and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
Romania is home to Europe's largest population of brown bears.
Romanian is the closest living language to Latin.

RU.name: Russia
facts: Russia is the largest country in the world, spanning 11 time zones.
Lake Baikal in Russia holds 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater.
The Moscow Metro is famous for its palatial stations with chandeliers, mosaics, and marble.
Russia sent the first human (Yuri Gagarin) and the first satellite (Sputnik) into space.
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world at 9,289 km.

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
facts: Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers — it's the largest country in the world without one.
Saudi Arabia is home to Mecca and Medina, the two holiest cities in Islam.
The country has the world's largest sand desert — the Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter).
Saudi Arabia allowed women to drive starting in 2018.
The country holds about 16% of the world's proven petroleum reserves.

SN.name: Senegal
facts: Senegal is known as the 'Gateway to Africa' due to its westernmost location on the continent.
Dakar was the finishing point of the famous Paris-Dakar Rally for decades.
Senegal's Lac Rose (Pink Lake) has waters that turn bright pink due to algae.
Teranga, meaning 'hospitality,' is a core cultural value in Senegal.
Senegal has never had a military coup, making it one of Africa's most stable democracies.

SG.name: Singapore
facts: Singapore is both a city and a country — one of only three city-states in the world.
Chewing gum has been banned in Singapore since 1992.
Singapore's Changi Airport has been voted the world's best airport for years running.
Despite its small size, Singapore is one of the world's busiest ports.
Singapore has four official languages: English, Malay, Mandarin, and Tamil.

ZA.name: South Africa
facts: South Africa has 11 official languages — more than almost any country.
South Africa is the only country to have voluntarily dismantled its nuclear weapons.
The first successful heart transplant was performed in Cape Town by Dr. Christiaan Barnard in 1967.
Table Mountain in Cape Town is one of the oldest mountains in the world — over 600 million years old.
South Africa has the third-largest biodiversity in the world.

ES.name: Spain
facts: Spain's La Tomatina festival involves throwing over 150,000 tomatoes in a town-wide food fight.
Spain has the second-highest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites in the world.
The Spanish Steps are actually in Rome — but the Spanish language is the 4th most spoken in the world.
Spain's tradition of siesta (afternoon nap) is still practiced in many regions.
The Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882.

SE.name: Sweden
facts: Sweden hasn't been at war since 1814 — the longest period of peace for any European nation.
IKEA, Spotify, and Minecraft were all created in Sweden.
Sweden recycles so well it has to import garbage from other countries to fuel its waste-to-energy plants.
The Nobel Prizes (except Peace) are awarded in Stockholm.
Sweden has the right of public access ('Allemansrätten') allowing anyone to roam freely in nature.

CH.name: Switzerland
facts: Switzerland has four official languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh.
Switzerland hasn't been in a war since 1815, maintaining armed neutrality.
The country has enough nuclear bunker space to shelter its entire population.
The Swiss consume more chocolate per capita than any other nation — about 10 kg per person per year.
Switzerland's flag is one of only two square sovereign-state flags (the other is Vatican City).

TH.name: Thailand
facts: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian country never colonized by a European power.
Bangkok's full ceremonial name is 168 characters long — the longest city name in the world.
Thailand was known as Siam until 1939.
Muay Thai (Thai boxing) is the national sport and a major cultural tradition.
Thailand is the world's largest exporter of rice.

TR.name: Turkey
facts: Istanbul is the only city in the world that spans two continents — Europe and Asia.
Turkey introduced coffee to Europe — the word 'coffee' comes from the Turkish 'kahve.'
The ancient city of Troy, from Homer's Iliad, was located in modern Turkey.
Turkey has more ancient Greek ruins than Greece itself.
Santa Claus (Saint Nicholas) was born in Patara, in modern-day Turkey.

UA.name: Ukraine
facts: Ukraine is the largest country entirely within Europe.
Kyiv's metro system includes one of the deepest stations in the world — Arsenalna at 105.5 meters.
Ukraine's flag represents blue sky over golden wheat fields.
The Chernobyl exclusion zone has become an unintentional wildlife refuge.
Ukraine is one of the world's largest exporters of sunflower oil.

AE.name: UAE
facts: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest building in the world at 828 meters.
The UAE has the world's first 3D-printed office building.
Dubai's Palm Jumeirah is the world's largest artificial island.
The UAE went from a desert economy to one of the wealthiest nations in just 50 years.
The UAE has seven emirates, each with its own ruler.

GB.name: United Kingdom
facts: The British Empire was the largest empire in history, covering about 25% of the world's land.
London's Big Ben is actually the name of the bell, not the clock tower.
The UK invented the World Wide Web — Tim Berners-Lee created it in 1989.
The Queen's Guard at Buckingham Palace are active soldiers who can arrest you.
English is spoken as a first or second language by over 1.5 billion people worldwide.

US.name: United States
facts: The US has no official language at the federal level.
Alaska is simultaneously the most northern, western, and eastern state (the Aleutian Islands cross the 180° meridian).
The US interstate highway system requires that one mile in every five must be straight — allegedly to serve as emergency airstrips.
The Library of Congress is the largest library in the world with over 170 million items.
Yellowstone National Park sits on top of a supervolcano.

VN.name: Vietnam
facts: Vietnam is the world's largest exporter of cashews and second-largest coffee exporter.
Halong Bay has nearly 2,000 limestone islands and islets.
Vietnam has the world's largest cave — Sơn Đoòng — large enough to fit a 40-story skyscraper.
Motorbikes outnumber cars 20:1 in Vietnam.
Vietnamese is a tonal language with six different tones.

TZ.name: Tanzania
facts: Mount Kilimanjaro, the tallest mountain in Africa, is in Tanzania.
The Serengeti hosts the largest annual migration of animals on Earth.
Zanzibar, part of Tanzania, was once the world's leading clove producer.
Tanzania is home to the Olduvai Gorge, one of the most important paleoanthropological sites.
Tanzanite, a precious gemstone, is found only in Tanzania.

VE.name: Venezuela
facts: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world at 979 meters.
Venezuela has the largest proven oil reserves in the world.
Lightning strikes over Lake Maracaibo up to 300 nights per year — a phenomenon called Catatumbo Lightning.
Venezuela is named after Venice ('Little Venice') by European explorers.
Venezuela has won more international beauty pageant titles than almost any other country.
